title: The Enochian Alphabet: the twenty-one forms of Sloane MS 3188, f. 104, drawn as type on their ink and set on one baseline
format: filled glyphs ({ fill }), glyphkit/README.md "Filled glyphs": absolute M L C Q Z, every subpath closed, fill-rule evenodd, viewBox 0 0 100 100, ink inside x 10-90, y 15-85

primary.copy: British Library, Sloane MS 3188, f. 104 (folio and date as given in the Wikimedia Commons description), reproduced on Wikimedia Commons as "File:Enochian letters (1583 manuscript).png": the uploaded original, 4303 x 1603 px, SHA-1 7f5476cdb427b9b9a37e06c4b82e00df9c2fd086 (matching the checksum on the Commons file page). Commons gives the manuscript as its source but not who made the image or where it was taken from; the image is essentially bitonal (thresholded), so solid ink carries no tonal detail.
primary.work: John Dee's record of his actions with spirits (the Libri Mysteriorum; Sloane MS 3188 holds the conferences of 22 December 1581 to 1583), the record of 6 May 1583: Dee's drawing of the twenty-one letters as Edward Kelley reported them, introduced by Dee's note "... there remayned only the shape of the letter in blak. after this manner. / and iust of this quantitie and proportion." (tentative reading of the crop).
primary.locator: f. 104: under three lines of Dee's English note, two lines of forms - 11 above (with a smaller second form written over the 2nd from the right) and 10 below - read from right to left; no names or Latin values stand beside the forms on this crop. Whitby's transcription puts the drawing at f. 104a, lines 30-31 (source report).
primary.why: Dee's note above the letters asks for the shape of the letter in black 'iust of this quantitie and proportion' (Whitby's transcription, as read in the source report); of the reachable images this original is the largest and sharpest (letters 142-212 px tall) and every form is whole in it.

witnesses.copy: British Library, Sloane MS 3189 (Liber Loagaeth), 'r. 57' per Commons; Wikimedia Commons "File:Enochian letters (1583 manuscript) alt.jpg", the 1085 x 441 px greyscale original (SHA-1 cd460a4ec63a9fc8f7678e552b67fb7124b94ea3); letters about 40-52 px tall.
witnesses.use: registered onto each f. 104 cell to read the course of strokes where f. 104 is solid: the course on which the crossings of Un and Or are drawn open, and Pal's dot, set clear of its stem; no outline taken from it

witnesses.copy: Meric Casaubon (ed.), A True & Faithful Relation (London, 1659), engraved Holy Table, Wellcome Collection copies 1 and 2 (IIIF full-resolution PNGs, Public Domain Mark).
witnesses.use: compared for the parts of Un, Or and Ged; its cutting of Un and Or agrees with the course on which their crossings are drawn open; no outline taken from it

scale.note: One scale for all 21 letters: 3.75 px of the 4303-px original to one unit of the 0-100 box (cell 375 px square), so their relative sizes and proportions are those of f. 104. Each cell is centred horizontally on its letter's ink box; vertically, both lines of f. 104 stand on one baseline at y 72.53 (see baseline), and each letter is drawn there. The fills are then set on a common baseline (see set).

baseline.note: One common baseline: each line's band runs from the median top to the median bottom (its baseline) of its letters' ink on f. 104, and both baselines are set at y 72.53, chosen so that the taller band, the upper line's, is centred on y 50. Every letter keeps its height above its own line's baseline, as on the page, and all 21 stand on one baseline. (The lines were first registered by the centres of their bands, which put the lower line's baseline 4 px of the original, 1.07 units, above the upper line's; corrected by the independent check, which moved the ten lower-line letters down by exactly 4 px, their outlines otherwise unchanged.)

upper_line.letters: Pa Veh Ged Gal Or Un Graph Tal Gon Na Ur (read right to left)

lower_line.letters: Mals Ger Drux Pal Med Don Ceph Van Fam Gisg (read right to left)

set.note: Each letter, drawn where its ink stands in its cell, is moved straight up or down (its shape unchanged) so that the set stands on one baseline as type: flat feet on y 71.0, round and pointed bottoms dipping to about y 71.6, and the parts that reach below the line on the leaf hanging below it (Un's drop, Ur's tail, Gisg's broad end, Mals's left serif, Fam's stem, Drux's end). Fam, whose stem hangs, is set by its top bar on the others' head line. Un, Ur and Gisg are not moved. Each letter's set.dy_units gives its move (positive down); the largest is Mals's, 5.3 units.

method: Cells: one 375-px square per letter from the 4303-px original, all at one scale (3.75 px to a unit), both lines on one baseline at y 72.53 (see baseline).

The ink: the letter's own connected ink in its cell, thresholded at 128 from a 4x bilinear enlargement, specks dropped, as a signed distance field; its medial axis gave the course of every stroke, and the ink across each node its width.

Construction (each letter's 'construction', in the cell's coordinates): strokes laid by hand on that axis, each a centre line through its nodes [x, y, width] or [x, y, left, right] (a centripetal Catmull-Rom spline, or straight with line: true), its width the ink's own across that node, interpolated monotonically along it, and its ends cut (cut, at a screen angle), flared to a wedge (flare: the half-widths grown on a concave curve over len units, then cut), rounded, or tapered to a point; where a part is not a stroke (a head, a foot, a lobe, a wedge, a bracket), its edge read off the ink's edge as runs of points ('runs': each run a smooth curve through its points, or a straight edge if it has two, the runs meeting at corners); Pal's dot an ellipse [cx, cy, rx, ry, rotation]; 'sub' parts cut away (Graph's outer corner, rounded as the ink is). The parts are united and the outline fitted with cubic Beziers whose on-curve points stand at corners, at the ends of straight edges and at the extrema of x and y, tangent-continuous elsewhere (within 0.1 unit of the union).
Weights: the ink's own, stroke by stroke, swelling and tapering where the ink does; the relative sizes and proportions of the letters are the leaf's.
Set: each letter moved straight up or down onto a common baseline (see set, and each letter's set).

Checked (each letter's 'check', on the outline before it is set): both ways against the raw ink, sampled every 0.1 unit, the outline's distance from the ink's edge and the ink edge's distance from the outline (95th percentile, maximum, and the share within 1 and within 3 units), the fill's area against the ink's, and their intersection over union. In every letter both distances keep within 3 units everywhere, the outline is within 1 unit of the ink's edge along at least 85 per cent of its length, and the intersection over union is at least 0.86. Also the kit's check.mjs on the fills as set, each letter's outline laid over its ink before the move, and the letters set in lines at 20, 32, 40, 64 and 96 px.

Departures from f. 104, and only these: Un's crossing and foot and Or's short strokes and foot, solid ink in the image, drawn open on the course Sloane MS 3189 and Casaubon's Holy Table (1659) give them (formConfidence medium); the dot of Pal set clear of its stem where Sloane MS 3189 has it, at f. 104's size (see its check); and the set on one baseline. No outline was taken from either witness.

The owner's reference images (a chart, a commercial SVG pack and a FontSpace font) were looked at for the level of finish and to cross-check which form is which letter; no outline was traced, copied or adapted from them.
previous: The type pass of commit 511d6c1: strokes on the same axes but of set weights (stems and bowls about 9.5, heavy bars 7.5), on the leaf's places; it departed from the ink's weights and from parts of its shape (Veh's lobe and head, Graph's stem and corner, Ceph's stem, Ger's uprights, Gal's base, Ged's hook and others), and set Pal's dot larger.
The filled outlines of commit 3f4f459: the ink's own edge, faired within a unit of it (kept in the git history of enochian.js).
Before that, centre-line glyphs { d } for the house pen traced from Wikimedia's 1920-px rendering of the same file.

letters.name: Un
letters.strokes: Filled outline of a zigzag: a heavy spine from the head at the upper left (a pointed lead-in, with an end rising beside it) down to the right and sharply back down to the left, full at the outer corner of the turn; an arm from the upper spine to a broad flared serif at the upper right; a bar across the lower bend from a point at the left, hooked up, then down to a broad spur at the lower right; a broad foot cut square at the left, with a drop below; the crossings open.
letters.formReason: its crossing, solid on f. 104, drawn open on the course of Sloane MS 3189

letters.variants: Sloane MS 3189: the same crossed form, more compact and heavier, the knot at the foot as dense. Casaubon 1659, Holy Table (e.g. bottom border, 1st box; the same in Wellcome copy 2): cut as a clean zigzag, down to the right and back down to the left, with a short serifed bar across each end; Dee's bent head, hooked right arm and heavy foot are regularised away. In the heading of Casaubon's Specimen the A of 'Pagesgem' (read right to left) is a different crossed form, an oblique stem hooked to the upper right and crossed at its foot, and both A's of 'Bacap' are y-like: the heading does not use the f. 104 form.

letters.name: Pa
letters.strokes: Filled outline: a heavy diagonal cut flat at the top, its head running out to a point at the upper left over a rounded underside, narrowing to the blunt point of a V; the thinner right arm climbs, curls over to the right and back across the top, and ends in a broad block hanging inside the curl, cut flat below; a small barb juts left where the curl leaves the arm; the inside of the V narrows to a point.

letters.variants: Sloane MS 3189: the same V with the right arm curled, the curl drawn as a nearly closed loop. Casaubon 1659: a V with a curled arm, its curl a small closed loop, stands in the left border of the Holy Table (boxes 75-76, Wellcome copy 1; in copy 2 the left border lies in the binding fold) and, set diagonally, in all four corner boxes; the plate does not name it. In the heading of Casaubon's Specimen the B of 'Bacap' (read right to left) is the same V with the right arm curled.

letters.name: Veh
letters.strokes: Filled outline: an upright stem whose flat head swells to the left on a concave curve and runs out to a blunt point at the left, standing on a foot cut flat, with a square toe at the right and a long reach to the left ending in a small hook; on the right a solid upper lobe, entered from below by a narrow notch, its end hanging inside, coming back to the stem at mid-height; a thin bar from mid-stem running on as a broad wing that rises to the upper right; and a lower bowl curling back up inside itself.
letters.formReason: a smaller second form, without the wing, stands above it on f. 104

letters.name: Gal
letters.strokes: Filled outline: a heavy head at the upper left running down to a point at the lower left, from which a bar runs right and bends down into a curved spine like a reversed C, lighter as it descends; an arm sweeping up to a round knob that curls down at the upper right; at the foot of the spine a heavy wedge pointed down at the lower right and out to the right, and from it a thin base, its underside arched up under the spine, running back left to a forked end, a rounded lobe above a point.

letters.name: Pal
letters.strokes: Filled outline: a top bar from a blunt end at the left, with a small head rising where the stem meets it, widening to a broad wedge at the right whose underside curves down to a point, its upper corner raised; an upright stem from under the bar’s left part, light at the top and widening to a foot splayed both ways; and a separate oval dot under the bar, to the right of the stem, standing clear of both.
